pictures.scene: Circle of Rembrandt, The Man with the Golden Helmet — the old soldier under the great embossed helmet with his face turned down into its shadow, for the choirmaster a Maskil of David after Doeg the Edomite went to Saul, why do you boast of evil O mighty man
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_circle_the_man_with_the_golden_helmet

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Return of the Prodigal Son — the father's two hands laid on the back of the son who has come home ragged, the loving devotion of God endures all day long, your tongue devises destruction
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_return_of_the_prodigal_son

pictures.scene: Jacques-Louis David, The Oath of the Horatii — the three bare blades held up together in the father's fist while the sons reach for them, like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit
pictures.name: pd_david_the_oath_of_the_horatii

pictures.scene: Follower of Hieronymus Bosch, The Conjurer — the trickster working his cups on the table while his partner lifts the purse of the man bent over watching, you love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking truth
pictures.name: pd_bosch_the_conjurer

pictures.scene: Frans Hals, Malle Babbe — the woman roaring with laughter over her tankard with the owl set on her shoulder, Selah, you love every word that devours
pictures.name: pd_hals_malle_babbe

pictures.scene: John Martin, The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah — the fire coming down on the cities of the plain and the whole sky burning over them, O deceitful tongue, surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin
pictures.name: pd_martin_sodom_and_gomorrah

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, The Jewish Cemetery — the tombs standing among the broken trees and the ruin under a torn sky, He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent, He will uproot you from the land of the living
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_the_jewish_cemetery

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Raising of Lazarus — Christ with His hand lifted over the opened grave while the onlookers fall back in fear, Selah, the righteous will see and fear
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_raising_of_lazarus

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Haman Recognizes His Fate — the man who built the gallows walking out from the table with the sentence already on his face, they will mock the evildoer saying, look at the man
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_haman_recognizes_his_fate

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Parable of the Rich Fool — the old man counting his gold by candlelight among the money bags and the ledgers at night, who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_parable_of_the_rich_fool

pictures.scene: Thomas Cole, The Course of Empire: Desolation — the one column left standing with a bird's nest on its capital above the drowned colonnades of the empire, and strengthened himself by destruction, but I am like an olive tree
pictures.name: pd_cole_the_course_of_empire_desolation

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Olive Trees — the old olives rooted in the bright field with their branches full of leaf, flourishing in the house of God, I trust in the loving devotion of God
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_olive_trees

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, The Ghent Altarpiece, The Singing Angels — the company of angels crowded over the open book with their mouths open in song, forever and ever, I will praise You forever
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_the_singing_angels

pictures.scene: Gerrit Dou, Praying Old Woman — the old woman with her hands pressed together over the closed book and her eyes shut, because You have done it, I will wait on Your name
pictures.name: pd_dou_praying_old_woman

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, The Ghent Altarpiece, The Adoration of the Lamb — the Lamb standing on the altar in the green meadow with the angels kneeling around it and the saints coming in from every side, for it is good, in the presence of Your saints
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_the_adoration_of_the_lamb

lines.text: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of David. After Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.”
Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man?
The loving devotion of God endures all day long.
Your tongue devises destruction
like a sharpened razor,
O worker of deceit.
You love evil more than good,
falsehood more than speaking truth.
Selah
You love every word that devours,
O deceitful tongue.
Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin;
He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent;
He will uproot you from the land of the living.
Selah
The righteous will see and fear;
they will mock the evildoer, saying,
“Look at the man
who did not make God his refuge,
but trusted in the abundance of his wealth
and strengthened himself by destruction.”
But I am like an olive tree
flourishing in the house of God;
I trust in the loving devotion of God
forever and ever.
I will praise You forever,
because You have done it.
I will wait on Your name—
for it is good—
in the presence of Your saints.
